qAndA.question: What color are the lines representing the paths in the library layout?
What visual cue indicates the presence of more pheromone on a path?
What happens to the ant's trail over time?

qAndA.answer: It retains more pheromone due to the shorter travel time and lower pheromone volatilization.
qAndA.question: Why is a shorter path more likely to be chosen by subsequent ants?

qAndA.answer: It efficiently identifies the shortest path through an emergent and iterative process.
qAndA.question: What is the main advantage of the ant colony algorithm for pathfinding?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: This video describes the end colony algorithm for searching the shortest path in LPSS.
Imagine an ant has directions to choose in a library, although sometimes it just choose
away randomly. It were more likely to choose the direction with more fereumum, which is
a kind of marking smell. And the ant will also release its own smell when moving. The smell
of each ant will be lighter and lighter as time goes on. Each part of path will be forgotten
unless another ant passes it. Since the short-term path costs less time, it has higher
probability to maintain the smell, so that it can lead the next ant. So the fereum on
each path has constant volatile rate. The longer the path is, the more fereumum will
be volatile. So, shorter path always has a higher probability to rest do more fereumum.
And that is why we can finally get the shortest path.

youtube_description:
This video explains how the ant colony algorithm works (in Library Path Searching System project).
It is an AI web project by students at University of Liverpool (2012).
The project can be found at https://github.com/jiazhewang/LPSS
Thanks for watching!
